basis: Biphasic encephalopathy with seizures and cerebral white-matter injury; infection is a trigger, not an intrinsic infectious diagnosis.
Adenocarcinoma arising in the stomach.
Hereditary corticospinal degeneration; skeletal muscle atrophy in 3/3 assessed patients supports common muscle involvement.
Primary proximal muscular dystrophy; cardiac and respiratory involvement are subtype-dependent and not established in most patients across this umbrella.
Respiratory-chain metabolic disorder; language delay in 4/4 and dystonia in 3/4 support neurologic involvement. Muscle biochemical findings alone do not establish clinical myopathy.
Mitochondrial disease with infantile striatal degeneration. Retinal dysfunction and muscle histology lack frequencies; ophthalmoparesis may reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Brain malformation, intellectual disability, severe myopia and brachytelephalangy define syndrome; dental and palatal abnormalities occur in 80-99%. Hair and nail findings are cosmetic.
Benign neoplasm confined to breast tissue, which is outside the 13 axes.
Fibronectin deposition damages renal glomeruli; secondary hypertension and renal acidosis do not establish additional organ disease.
Congenital structural skeletal myopathy; cardiomegaly and congestive heart failure in 1/2 patients support cardiac involvement. Respiratory weakness does not establish lung injury.
Atrial electrical rhythm disorder.
Genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; hypotonia and cerebral visual impairment reflect nervous-system dysfunction.

Infantile neurodegeneration and optic atrophy define syndrome; generalized muscle atrophy occurs in 4/4 assessed patients. Aspiration and restrictive ventilation do not establish intrinsic lung damage.
Congenital long-QT arrhythmia and profound sensorineural deafness define syndrome; iron deficiency anemia is occasional.
Hydrocephalus and posterior fossa malformations accompany a defining cutaneous capillary malformation. Eyelid nevus does not establish ocular dysfunction.
Developmental disability, cardiac defect and anal atresia define syndrome; ocular ptosis is also a defining feature, retained as involved because primary is capped at three.
Respiratory-chain disorder; cognitive impairment and sensorimotor neuropathy in 1/1 patient support neurologic involvement. Muscle enzyme deficiency alone does not establish clinical myopathy.
Congenital cystic dilation of the distal ureter within the bladder; both belong to the renal axis.
Inherited peripheral neuropathy; chronic distal muscle wasting and associated foot deformities affect most patients, supporting musculoskeletal involvement.
Squamous cell carcinoma arising in skin; spindle-cell morphology does not change its organ of origin.
Neoplasm involving the lumbar peripheral nerve plexus.
Carcinoma involving the duodenum; no additional organ involvement is inherent to this umbrella.
Inherited restrictive myocardial disease; systemic manifestations of particular listed subtypes do not apply across this umbrella.
Benign smooth-muscle neoplasm arising within a bronchus; airway origin determines the axis.
Paraneoplastic dysfunction of the digestive system; the broad definition does not establish an immune mechanism or another affected organ.
